messages:
maria: Quick thread to lock ServeFlow sprint scope and launch gates. We have 3 customer asks (AtlasPay, Borealis, FinSaaS) and a few internal perf targets. Need final PRD checklist and owners.
ashwin: Suggest we split into two streams: (A) KV eviction + pinning API, (B) kernel selection + routing. Attention micro-ops can be feature-flagged and decoupled.
joel: I second. KV is highest risk for customers with long context. Proposal for eviction algo: tenant-sharded segmented-LRU, with explicit pin set per-tenant and a pinned-lease TTL.
sophia: For validation we need: short-seq QoR suite (<=512), long-seq QoR suite (4k-16k), and perf traces that mimic AtlasPay load (many long chats, occasional spikes). Add these to CI.
tess: AtlasPay PM wants hard pins (never evict) for payment-context prefixes. They're asking: is hard pin permanent or subject to admin quotas?
ashwin: Hard pins must be quota-limited. Implementation: control-plane quota + an admin override for emergencies. Document per-tenant limit and per-org quota.
joel: Acceptance criteria for KV work: 1) p99 token latency no worse than baseline or improves by >=8% on heavy-eviction traces; 2) pinned keys must never be evicted during normal ops; 3) API to invalidate/purge specific keys works within 200ms.
sophia: Also require correctness tests: no stale-kv reads when model switches or during partial rollouts. Add unit + integration tests that simulate model swap concurrency.
maria: Kernel selection acceptance criteria: must reduce avg token latency for small-batch, short-seq cases by >=10% without increasing p99 by >4% for long-seq traffic. Also target <=2% token-cost delta.
ashwin: Heuristic for kernel mux: if batch_size <=4 AND avg_seq_len <=1024 -> use low-latency kernel; else use throughput kernel. But we must measure memory pressure and kv-compatibility.
joel: Edge case: low-latency kernel may not support quantized KV layout. Need capability negotiation and graceful fallback path to safe kernel at runtime.
sophia: Attention micro-op plan: initial optimized path for seq<1024 with fused qk matmul and streamed softmax. Gate behind per-tenant FF and runtime capability bit. Tests: measure QoR and numeric divergence vs fp32 for 1000 eval prompts.
tess: Launch gating from customers: AtlasPay requires staging pass + customer signoff. Borealis wants a 2-week shadow period on production traffic. FinSaaS is ok with canary+rollback.
maria: Proposed rollout gates: staging perf + QoR green for 48h -> staged canary 3% traffic for 24h with synthetic load -> 10% for 48h + production shadow for 72h -> full rollout. Abort if error rate delta >0.04% or p99 exceeds thresholds.
ashwin: Add automatic circuit-breaker: if model-fallback rate >0.5% OR kernel-fallback rate >0.2% revert canary traffic automatically. Keep human-in-loop for final revert.
joel: Migration strategy for KV format changes: prefer dual-read shim for backwards compat where feasible; otherwise drain+flush path with migration window. Include cost estimate (cpu-hours, risk) for both in RFC.
sophia: CI requirements: on each PR, run short+long evals, perf micro-benchmarks, and p95/p99 regression checks. Add a mandatory check for numeric divergence threshold. ci-bot should block merge on failures.
ci-bot: note: perf jobs may take longer; recommend running quick smoke first and schedule full perf in parallel.
maria: Security & multi-tenant isolation: runtime must enforce tenant namespaces for KV, separate caches, and scrub logs for pinned keys. Add audit events for pin/invalidate actions.
tess: For AtlasPay acceptance criteria, we're adding a hard-pin SLA doc. I'll coordinate legal & PM.
nashwin: Owners: I own the PRD (kernel mux perf matrix + canary plan), Joel owns KV design & runbook, Sophia owns eval harness and dashboards, Tess manages customer validation + API contract.
joel: I'll draft the canary orchestration runbook with k8s job for warmup, pre-warm hooks, and automated monitors (evictions/sec, cache-hit%, kernel-fallbacks).
maria: Risk register short list: (a) numeric divergence in quant kernels; (b) cache blowouts from mis-pinning; (c) rollout flaps causing customer errors. Mitigations: fp fallback, per-tenant pin quotas, automated rollback throttling.
sophia: Also add test vectors for sequence-trimming + pinned-prefix interactions (long-chat truncation must preserve pinned prefix).
maria: Timeline: PRD draft in 48h, RFC first pass in 96h, RFC review Thurs 10am PT. Please add links here when drafts are ready.
tess: I'll invite AtlasPay PM to Thurs review.
deploy-bot: scheduled: staging canary for kv-evict-v1 on Tue 03:00 UTC (3% traffic). Logs: <link://canary/2477659999>
maria: One open question: do we expose pin-by-hash vs pin-by-key? Pros/cons? Pin-by-hash is compact but less readable for customers. Add to RFC options.
joel: I'll write both options and recommended proto for API; include migration notes.
ashwin: Small ask: gate attention micro-ops behind a tenant opt-in for first 30 days. Helps us roll back without global impact.
sophia: agreed. We'll default-off for managed tenants.
maria: OK, locking scope. Thanks all.
